name: 2005 forum signature
summary: Wide crop, repeated heads, an oversized screen name.
sources: Choose a wide scene and a recognizable head or mascot with room beside it for a name.
composition: Crop the base to a wide strip with cutout(no_ai=true) when useful. Place one oversized subject to a side, then two or three smaller hard-edged copies. Keep the name readable in the remaining space.
typography: Use text(style=wordart) for the screen name and a short plain or paint tagline.
finish: Use modest save JPEG crunch; add a flare only when it supports the chosen brief. Avoid filling every gap.

name: Office WordArt disaster
summary: A crooked flyer with stretched lettering and misplaced badges.
sources: Choose a simple background, a subject cutout, and a small relevant emoji or clip-art-like object.
composition: Place a large tilted subject off center. Repeat a small badge or emoji in a corner. Leave a clear area for one oversized title instead of covering the subject.
typography: Mix a large text(style=wordart) title with a smaller text(style=paint) line. Uneven placement is intentional; clipped words are not.
finish: Use a slight squash through paste width/height and ordinary JPEG save. Keep the joke visible through the clutter.

name: Tabloid front page
summary: An enormous headline, an incriminating inset, and a red arrow.
sources: Choose one expressive main photo with headline space and one supporting photo or crop that advances the joke.
composition: Use a large main image; paste a smaller rectangular inset into a corner. Draw a red arrow or circle connecting the inset to the supposed evidence. Keep the main subject unobscured.
typography: Use a very short Impact top headline and a bottom punchline. A tiny inset label is optional, never a paragraph.
finish: Save with moderate JPEG crunch; avoid deep frying by default so the headline remains legible.

name: Bootleg DVD cover
summary: A crowded cast collage, a huge title, and too many taglines.
sources: Choose a tall dramatic background and two or three recognizable subjects with contrasting expressions or scales.
composition: Build a cast collage with one giant face high in the frame and smaller figures below. Hard rectangular seams and mismatched scales are welcome. Reserve the bottom quarter for the title.
typography: Use a large WordArt title, one exaggerated tagline above it, and a short paint-style endorsement at an odd angle if space permits.
finish: A single flare and mild color filter can support the brief. Keep facial features and the title readable after save.

name: Museum vandalism
summary: One absurd substitution in an otherwise serious painting.
sources: Choose a public-domain painting or statue image with a clear focal subject and a replacement whose pose fits the joke.
composition: Make one obvious substitution: replace a head, a held object, or one central figure. Preserve most of the original artwork so the contrast carries the joke.
typography: Usually omit captions. If requested, use one short museum-label-like plain line away from the altered subject.
finish: Use ordinary save. No default lasers, emoji rain, deep fry, or decorative clutter.

name: Conspiracy diagram
summary: Three pieces of evidence connected by increasingly absurd arrows.
sources: Choose two or three visually distinct objects or faces linked by the user's premise; seek clear silhouettes over busy scenery.
composition: Arrange separate rectangular evidence crops around the base with space between them. Connect them using draw arrows, circles, and lines. Make the central claim visibly distinct from the supporting scraps.
typography: Use short paint labels beside each item and one Impact question as the headline. Keep labels out of faces and arrows out of text.
finish: Save with light JPEG crunch. Restraint in the number of nodes makes the absurd relationship readable.
